# Nārāyaṇa Daśā — Padakrama Daśā of Jaimini: The Three-Śakti Architecture

## Where Nārāyaṇa Walks, The World Follows

Imagine Nārāyaṇa walking through your life. Every place his foot lands becomes the circumstance of that period — the job market that exists, the city you live in, the people available to meet, the weather of the years themselves. He doesn't ask whether you *want* the place; he just walks. Your job is to live there for the time he stays. Then he steps to the next sign, and a new world arrives around you, set by where he sits next.

That is Nārāyaṇa Daśā. A **Rāśi Daśā** — a sign-based timing system, not a planet-based one. Where graha-daśās (like Vimśottarī) tell you *who walks into your life* and when, Nārāyaṇa Daśā tells you *what landscape Nārāyaṇa has set you down inside*.[^1] The mind, the desire, the personal agenda — those are Vimśottarī's concern. The world that gets put in front of the mind — that is Nārāyaṇa.

Visti Larsen names this distinction sharply: *"The mind however is subservient to the circumstances laid before it... Even if you want a job, you will not get one unless jobs are available. The desire is caused by the mind, but Nārāyaṇa provides the availability."*[^2] Two daśās, two layers. You cannot read one without the other.

## What This Actually Is

The Daśā is called **Padakrama Daśā** in some lineages — *"the series of steps,"* or *"the series of quarters."* Pada is the quarter, and the steps Nārāyaṇa takes through the zodiac become quarters of your life. In the tradition of **Śrī Acyuta Dāsa** — which is the lineage Visti Larsen receives through Sanjay Rath — this Daśā is called **Nārāyaṇa Daśā** specifically because *it encompasses the three types of śakti said to reside in Nārāyaṇa*.[^3]

The three śakti are:

| Śakti | Goddess | Sign-Type |
|---|---|---|
| **Śrī Śakti** | Mahā Lakṣmī | Movable signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn) |
| **Bhū Śakti** | Mahā Sarasvati | Fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius) |
| **Nīla Śakti** | Mahā Kāli | Dual signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) |

The architecture is theological before it is technical. Nārāyaṇa contains three goddess-energies. The zodiac contains three sign-types. The three sign-types *are* the three goddess-energies expressed as terrain. When Nārāyaṇa's foot lands on a movable sign, you are in Lakṣmī's quarter — wealth-pulse, motion, expansion. On a fixed sign, Sarasvati — accumulated wisdom, immobile depth. On a dual sign, Kāli — transition, dissolution, change-of-state. Read this way, the Daśā is not a calendar. It is a sequence of goddess-rooms you walk through.

This page does not teach the calculation itself — Larsen explicitly defers that to Sanjay Rath's *Nārāyaṇa Daśā*.[^4] What this page locks is the **interpretive grammar**: how the Daśā is read once it has been calculated.

## The Mechanism: Treating the Daśā Rāśi as Lagna

Larsen's foundational interpretive move is simple and unfamiliar at the same time. *Take the Daśā Rāśi as if it were the Lagna.* Read planets from that sign as you would read planets from the birth-Lagna.[^5] The whole horoscope re-orients around the sign Nārāyaṇa now occupies.

Behind the Three-Śakti naming sits a parallel Trinity-governance Larsen leaves implicit and Rao makes explicit. The three sign-types are *each governed by one face of the Hindu Trinity in their progression-mode*: movable rāśis are governed by Brahmā (creation, where Nārāyaṇa starts new cycles), fixed rāśis are governed by Shiva (the "every 6th" progression-rule applies to fixed dasa-seeds because Shiva's destruction-rhythm cuts every sixth step), and dual rāśis are governed by Vishnu (sustenance, the dual-sign holds both motion and stability). The Three-Śakti theological-architecture (Lakṣmī/Sarasvati/Kāli = Bhū-essences) sits alongside this Trimūrti governance-architecture in the same daśā — Rao calculates the progression-rule from the Trinity-governance layer, the goddess-quarter quality is then experienced inside that progression.[^12] The technical-operational layer is Trimūrti-governed; the experiential-quality layer is Three-Śakti-coded. Both run simultaneously, neither reducible to the other.

The progression-rule contains two named exceptions that significantly alter the calculation: the **Saturn exception** and the **Ketu exception**. If Saturn occupies the dasa seed (the sign from which Nārāyaṇa Daśā begins), apply Saturn-exception progression rules instead of the normal sequence. If Ketu occupies the dasa seed, apply Ketu-exception rules. The exceptions exist because Saturn (the great-malefic) and Ketu (the moksa-graha) each *re-route Nārāyaṇa's walking path* in characteristic ways — Saturn stalls and reverses; Ketu cuts the path short. Three progression-cases per dasa seed (normal / Saturn-exception / Ketu-exception) must be checked before computing the full Daśā schedule. A practitioner who ignores the exceptions and runs the normal progression on a Saturn-seed or Ketu-seed chart produces *off-schedule predictions* with cascading error across the full 120-year-equivalent Nārāyaṇa-calendar. The exceptions are not edge-cases — Saturn or Ketu in dasa-seed occurs in roughly 16% of charts statistically (2/12 + node-conditional).

The principles transpose cleanly:
- Benefics in 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 10th, 12th from the Daśā Rāśi = auspicious.
- Malefics in 3rd and 6th from the Daśā Rāśi = auspicious. Benefics in those houses are not.
- Any planet in the 9th or 11th = auspicious.[^6]

A quiet inversion runs underneath this. Benefics in the 8th from the Daśā Rāśi are auspicious — counter to most natal interpretations where 8H placement is feared. The Daśā-as-Lagna re-reads the 8th as the *inner-wealth-vault* the Daśā opens, and benefics there protect that vault. The same flip applies to malefics in 6H: from natal Lagna 6H-malefics often cause illness, but from Daśā Rāśi they sharpen the native's combat-edge for that period.

Within that frame, individual placements lock specific outcomes:
- Malefics in the 4th — change of home, leaving the familiar.
- Malefics in the 2nd or 8th — money strain, bad loans respectively.
- Malefics in the 3rd or 6th — aggressive posture, success in battles (unless debilitated).
- Saturn in the 7th from Daśā Rāśi — *"few desires, will be lazy and will sleep late."*[^7] The desire-engine itself dampens for that period.

The seventh from the Daśā Rāśi is read as the **desire-direction** for that period — what the native *will want* during the Daśā, not what natal 7H promised at birth. This is one of the deepest re-orientations Larsen teaches: desire itself is daśā-coloured. You are not the same wanting-self across periods.

## The Three-Part Daśā Trend (Sign-Rising-Type Architecture)

Each Mahādaśā divides into three equal portions. Which portion delivers which kind of result depends on **how the sign rises** — its astronomical posture.

| Sign-Rising-Type | 1st Portion | 2nd Portion | 3rd Portion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Śīrṣodaya** (rises with head) | Sign-effects | — | — |
| **Ubhayodaya** (Pisces, rises both ways) | — | Sign-effects | — |
| **Pṛṣṭhodaya** (rises with back) | — | — | Sign-effects |

The remaining two slots (lord-effects and occupants/aspects) fill the empty portions according to a deferral logic: **malefic lords give their results later in the Daśā; benefic lords give them earlier.** Occupants and aspects typically fill the middle.[^8]

The mechanism is structural. A sign that "rises with its head" enters consciousness immediately — you feel the sign's *quality* first when Nārāyaṇa steps onto it. A sign that "rises with its back" announces itself slowly — the sign-quality arrives only after the lord's actions and the occupants' interventions have already played. Pisces, the dual-rising-both-ways sign, holds its quality in the middle as a balance point.

The Bush worked example (Pisces Mahādaśā 2000-2006) is the textbook case.[^9] Pisces is Ubhayodaya. The first portion (2000-2002) gave the *lord's* results — Jupiter in Māraṇa Kāraka Sthāna, forming Gaja-Kesarī with the Moon. The election court-case (Jupiter = judges) and the September 11 attacks fell here. The middle portion (2002-2004) gave the *sign's* results — Pisces as the 9th house, foreign travel, war on Iraq. The third portion (2004-2006) gave the *occupants/aspects'* results — Moon aspecting Pisces, fame, the 2004 election win. The three-part architecture predicted the *order* of the events, not just their presence.

## Synergies & Handshakes Inside the Vault

This page is the upstream half of a triad. Read in sequence with [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/dvara-bahya-paka-bhoga-4-reference-points-larsen|Dvāra/Bāhya/Pāka/Bhoga 4 Reference Points]] (which deepens the *within-Mahādaśā* reading) and [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/vimshottari-7-positions-jataka-parijata-18-33|Vimśottarī 7 Positions]] (which complements with the mind-layer), the three together form Larsen's complete daśā stack.

It hands directly to [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/visti-larsen-pancanga-keystone-methodology|Pañcāṅga Keystone Methodology]] — Nārāyaṇa Daśā operates downstream of the Pañcāṅga karma-filter. The Pañcāṅga determines *what kind of karma is available to ripen at all*; the Nārāyaṇa Daśā schedules *when each parcel ripens*.

It connects to [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/multi-lagna-interpretive-sphere-4-tier|Multi-Lagna 4-Tier Interpretive Sphere]] — the Daśā-Rāśi-as-Lagna technique adds a fifth interpretive vantage to the existing four, but only operationally for the period in question. The vantage *moves* as Nārāyaṇa walks.

It pulls against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/jyotish-as-karma-trigger-model|Jyotiṣa as Karma-Trigger Model]] — Nārāyaṇa Daśā is *the* paradigmatic karma-trigger device. The native doesn't generate the new circumstance; the circumstance arrives because Nārāyaṇa walked there.

## Analytical Case Study: John Kerry's Leo Daśā 1996-2005

Kerry's Leo Nārāyaṇa Daśā ran 1996-2005.[^10] Leo is Śīrṣodaya — rises with its head — so sign-effects in the first portion, occupants/aspects in the middle, lord (Sun) in the third.

**First portion, 1996-1999** — sign-effects. Leo houses Jupiter. Good name, reputation, fifth-house support of Mercury (communications). The early Senate years.

**Middle portion, 1999-2002** — occupants/aspects. Jupiter conjoined other planets, fifth-and-second lord in the 10th from Lagna, joined Ārūḍha Lagna. Fame climbed. Venus's aspect from the 12th gave śubha yoga and an act of *renunciation* — Kerry stepped back from the 2000 Democratic primary because Al Gore was running. Ketu's Rāśi-dṛṣṭi on Leo from Capricorn made him courageous, lion-like — and through 9/11 he became one of the senators preparing the country for war. The Daśā's middle portion delivered exactly what the occupants/aspects coded.

**Third portion, 2002-2005** — Sun, the Daśā lord. Sun in the Lagna joined Ghaṭika Lagna and Horā Lagna — *rising to power*. Sun is the 10th lord. The 2004 presidential run. From the Daśā Rāśi the Sun moved to the 4th — caution, change of residence. Kerry won the Democratic nomination but lost the general election (Sun in the 8th from Ghaṭika Lagna was operating against retention of power; his opponent Bush had Sun in the Lagna).

Three portions, three pre-coded result-streams, all delivered in sequence. The case is a precision-test for the sign-rising-type rule. Larsen's read predicts the *temporal shape* of Kerry's decade, not just its themes.

## Implementation Workflow: A Tuesday Reading

A client sits across from you. Date of birth on the page. You have the chart open in two windows — Rāśi on the left, the Nārāyaṇa Daśā table on the right. The current Mahādaśā is highlighted: Capricorn, running 2024 through 2034 say. Ten years.

You don't start with planets. You start with the sign. Capricorn — Pṛṣṭhodaya, rises with its back. You make a note: *sign-effects in the last third*. The native is currently in 2026 — year two of the Daśā. The sign itself is not yet showing its hand. Whatever's happening to them now is the lord's work or the occupants' work, depending on which fills the front portion.

You look at Saturn (the lord). Saturn is benefic for this Lagna? Malefic? You check beneficence. Malefic lords give their results later, you remember. So Saturn likely runs in the middle third (2027-2030), and the occupants/aspects of Capricorn are what's running *now*. You look at Capricorn — Mars sits there, in the 4th from Lagna. Mars is what they're being put through right now. You ask about the home, about property, about a move.

The native says they bought a property in March and the family is at each other's throats over it. You nod. *Mars in the 4th, Daśā-Rāśi-as-Lagna,* you don't say. You ask about the property's location — north of the birthplace? They look surprised: yes. Mars in the 4th coded the move, and the direction was readable. The mid-Daśā portion hasn't even fully arrived yet — Saturn's results begin around 2027 and will reframe everything they think about home and family.

You write down the projection in your notebook: *sign-effects 2030-2033, Pṛṣṭhodaya-tail.* The sign Capricorn is the second house from Lagna — wealth and family-line. The final third of the Daśā will be where the wealth and lineage themes deliver. You tell the native what to prepare for: not yet, but in five years, expect the family-wealth question to surface as the dominant issue. They write that down too.

Read this way, the Daśā is not a prediction-machine. It is a **calendar of incoming worlds**, each pre-coded by the sign Nārāyaṇa now occupies. The job is to tell the native which world is arriving next, not whether they will succeed inside it.

## The Nārāyaṇa Daśā Failure (Diagnostic Signs)

Read at the wrong level, Nārāyaṇa Daśā disappoints. The failure modes have signatures:

- **Reading sign-effects across the whole Daśā when they belong to one third.** A Śīrṣodaya Daśā where you keep waiting for sign-effects to arrive in the middle. They already happened in the first third. You missed them.
- **Treating planetary placements from the natal Lagna instead of from the Daśā Rāśi.** The Daśā is not visible from the natal Lagna. Mars in the 6th from natal Lagna may bless health. Mars in the 6th from the *current Daśā Rāśi* will sharpen the native into a fighter for those years.
- **Ignoring the seventh-from-Daśā-Rāśi desire-direction.** The native says, "I don't know why I suddenly stopped wanting anything." You check the Daśā: Saturn sits in the seventh from the current sign. Of course. The desire-engine is shut down by Saturn's depressive seventh-house placement *for this period only*.
- **Mixing Nārāyaṇa Daśā with Vimśottarī as if they were redundant.** Larsen is explicit that they handle *different layers*. Nārāyaṇa = circumstance, the world Nārāyaṇa lays out. Vimśottarī = mind, the desire that meets the world. Both required.
- **Forgetting the deferral rule for aspecting lords.** Lord aspecting the Daśā Rāśi defers its effects to the *lord's portion*. The aspect doesn't mix into all three portions equally.

## Evidence / Tensions / Open Questions

The interpretive framework is sourced from Sanjay Rath's *Nārāyaṇa Daśā* and from Maharṣi Jaimini through Acyuta Dāsa.[^11] Larsen positions this Daśā at the top of the Rāśi-Daśā hierarchy for circumstantial timing, but is explicit that it does not replace Vimśottarī for mind-and-desire timing.

The three-śakti theological framing (Śrī / Bhū / Nīla = movable / fixed / dual) is *not* operationally invoked in most Larsen reads — it sits as the *naming-rationale* for the Daśā but is rarely worked at the predictive layer. Whether the three-śakti distinction has predictive content beyond sign-type-rising-rule is an **open question**. A native in a movable-sign Daśā is supposedly under Śrī Śakti's influence; does Lakṣmī-worship intensify the period's auspicious results in a way Sarasvati-worship would not? The text does not commit.

The seventh-from-Daśā-Rāśi as **desire-direction** is one of the deepest claims and is under-exploited in most practitioner reads. It deserves its own future cross-domain handshake with depth-psychology desire-as-state-dependent literature.

## Author Tensions & Convergences

Larsen on Nārāyaṇa Daśā runs *alongside* Sanjay Rath as both teacher and source, and that mostly suppresses the kind of disagreement an Author T&C section usually traffics in. The deeper interest is in how Larsen positions Nārāyaṇa Daśā relative to other lineages' keystone-daśās.

For [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/kurczak-fish-vedic-astrology|Kurczak and Fish]] (Kriya Yoga lineage), Vimśottarī is the operational keystone — the technical center of gravity is the 120-year planetary cycle and its sub-periods. Nārāyaṇa Daśā either does not appear or is treated as an adjunct. The result is a daśā-stack that reads the native primarily as a mind-with-desires moving through life-stages. The circumstances appear as a backdrop that the native's karma-mind activates, not as a separate Nārāyaṇa-laid-out terrain.

For Larsen, the circumstance comes first. Nārāyaṇa walks; you live where he walks. Vimśottarī is the *mind's response to the walking*. The order matters because it reframes what astrological prediction is *for* — Larsen's framework asks the native to *prepare for arriving circumstances*; Kurczak-Fish asks the native to *purify the mind that meets whatever circumstance comes*. Both pictures cover the same year, but they ask the native to do different work inside that year.

The reveal: the lineage's choice of *which daśā to put on top* encodes the lineage's theory of *where karma actually lives*. Larsen, downstream of Acyuta Dāsa via Rath, treats karma as primarily *circumstantial* — written into the world that arrives. Kurczak-Fish treats karma as primarily *mind-stuff* — written into the desires-and-aversions that meet whatever world arrives. Both are theologically defensible. The difference produces operationally distinct practices.

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

The Buddhist monk and the Stoic philosopher meet on the same ground when this Daśā is described to them. The monk says: *yes, that is exactly the structure of dependent origination — the world arrives because conditions ripened.* The Stoic says: *we cannot control fortune; we can only control our response to it.* And the modern systems theorist hears: *this is a state-machine where state-transitions are exogenous and only the agent's policy is endogenous.* Three vocabularies, one architecture. The Daśā handshakes outward in three directions.

- **Psychology**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/affect-as-context-dependent-state|Affect as Context-Dependent State]] — modern affective-science work locates emotion not in the brain alone but in the body-in-environment system, with context as a load-bearing variable. Nārāyaṇa Daśā encodes the same structural truth: the native is not the same wanting-self across periods because the *seventh-from-Daśā-Rāśi* (desire-direction) shifts with each Daśā. The Saturn-in-7H-from-Daśā-Rāśi flatness is not depression-as-pathology; it is *Daśā-coded reduced desire*. The handshake produces an insight neither field generates alone: clinical depression diagnoses may sometimes be misreading a Saturn-coded period as a personality defect. The Daśā stops in eight years; the native is not broken. The two-system view (mind + circumstance) gives the clinician a corrective frame the DSM does not.

- **Behavioral-Mechanics**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/timing-and-the-art-of-strategic-patience|Timing and the Art of Strategic Patience]] — Robert Greene's *33 Strategies of War* treats timing as a tactical resource: the strategist who knows *when not to act* outperforms the strategist who knows *what* to do. Nārāyaṇa Daśā provides a non-tactical version of the same insight — the native who knows *which sign Nārāyaṇa currently occupies* can refuse to act when the seventh-from-Daśā-Rāśi has Saturn and the desire-engine is shut down. Don't try to start a company in a Saturn-flattened desire-direction; the period itself is making you indifferent to outcomes. Wait two years. The handshake reveals the *tactical use of cosmological knowledge* — Daśā-aware action is a strategic advantage Greene's secular timing-frame approaches but does not reach.

- **History**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/history/great-man-vs-structural-conditions-debate|Great-Man vs. Structural-Conditions Debate]] — historiography divides on whether outcomes are driven by extraordinary individuals or by the structural conditions they happen to inhabit. Nārāyaṇa Daśā votes structural without surrendering the individual. The native does work, has agency, makes choices — but inside a Nārāyaṇa-laid terrain that is exogenously given. The handshake produces a third position the debate rarely articulates: *individual karma generates the terrain that future individuals must work inside*. Kerry's Leo Daśā delivered a 2004 candidacy because *Kerry's prior choices had built the conditions*, but the 2004 timing was Nārāyaṇa's walking schedule, not Kerry's calendar choice. The structural and the individual are not opposed; they are linked across lifetimes through the karma-substrate.

The three handshakes converge on a single deep claim: **the world that arrives is not random and is not chosen, but it can be read.** Read it, and act inside what is given. Refuse to read it, and you spend your life pushing against a Daśā Nārāyaṇa has already chosen to put in front of you.

## The Live Edge

**The Sharpest Implication**

If Nārāyaṇa Daśā is *real* — if the world that arrives in your fortieth year is a function of which sign Nārāyaṇa stepped onto when you turned thirty — then most life-coaching, self-improvement, and motivational discourse is solving the wrong half of the problem. You can purify your mind, sharpen your desires, optimize your habits all you like; the world that arrives is still the world Nārāyaṇa is walking. The corrective is not to abandon agency but to *match it to the terrain*. In a Saturn-7H-from-Daśā-Rāśi period, the mature move is not to push harder against your suddenly-absent desire-engine. The mature move is to sit. Wait. Read. The period ends.

**Generative Questions**

- The three-śakti theological framing (Śrī / Bhū / Nīla = movable / fixed / dual) has not been operationally tested. Does worship of Mahā Lakṣmī during a movable-sign Mahādaśā produce stronger results than worship of Mahā Sarasvati would? If yes, the framing is predictive; if no, it is purely classificatory. What would a chart-paired test look like?

- The seventh-from-Daśā-Rāśi as desire-direction is the most under-exploited reading-rule. How does the *desire-direction* interact with the natal seventh-house promise? Is there a chart where natal 7H promises a strong relationship-desire but Daśā-7H Saturn makes the native indifferent — and the native splits the difference by saying yes to relationship without wanting it?

- If Larsen's prioritization (circumstance first, mind second) maps onto Acyuta Dāsa's lineage, and Kurczak-Fish's prioritization (mind first, circumstance second) maps onto Kriya Yoga's lineage — does the lineage *itself* select practitioners whose own charts confirm the prioritization? Are Larsen's students predominantly natives whose Nārāyaṇa Daśā delivers clearer signals than their Vimśottarī? Does the framework attract the chart it best reads?

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/dvara-bahya-paka-bhoga-4-reference-points-larsen|Dvāra/Bāhya/Pāka/Bhoga Four Reference Points]] — the within-Mahādaśā four-point deepening of this Daśā
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/vimshottari-7-positions-jataka-parijata-18-33|Vimśottarī 7 Positions]] — the complementary mind-layer Daśā Larsen always pairs with this one
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/visti-larsen-pancanga-keystone-methodology|Pañcāṅga Keystone Methodology]] — upstream karma-filter that determines what kind of karma is available to ripen
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/multi-lagna-interpretive-sphere-4-tier|Multi-Lagna 4-Tier Interpretive Sphere]] — Daśā-Rāśi-as-Lagna adds a fifth, period-specific vantage
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/jyotish-as-karma-trigger-model|Jyotiṣa as Karma-Trigger Model]] — Nārāyaṇa Daśā is the paradigmatic karma-trigger device

This is contrary to the graha daśās, which revolve around the entry of other souls into our lives... The Nārāyaṇa Daśā is the movement of Nārāyaṇa through our lives."*

# Semblance Dharmas

## The Counterfeit You Built Yourself

There is a category of spiritual attainment that is not fake, not fraudulent, and not the real thing.

> Semblance dharmas are artificial cultivation attainments that mimic the real spiritual attainments because they **look almost exactly the same**, but which are not the real thing. Many in fact, are unnatural in that they **can only be maintained through force**.[^1]

Notice what is being described. Not a person pretending. Not a mistake about what happened. A state that genuinely occurred, that closely resembles the real one, that the practitioner produced — and that has to be held in place.

The word *semblance* is doing careful work. A semblance is not a lie; it is a likeness. And the trouble with a good likeness is that likeness is exactly what everyone is checking for.

## Where They Come From

The cause Bodri names is technique, and specifically a certain kind of technique.

> The prolonged use of **forceful form school techniques** may lead to various harmful attachments, and they can even end up producing misleading "semblance dharmas" rather than the genuine stages of cultivation gong-fu which are desired.[^1]

Forceful, form-based, prolonged. Methods that work on shapes — postures, breath counts, visualisations, retentions — pushed hard enough and long enough to produce something.

And they do produce something. That is the whole difficulty. A forced method that produced nothing would be self-correcting; a forced method that produces a convincing likeness of the goal is not.

He names the schools he thinks escaped it: Zen, and what he calls the authentic schools of Taoism and Esoteric Buddhism, which *avoided the use of any artificial cultivation techniques* and so usually bypassed the problem.[^1] The parenthesis he adds is worth keeping — *but not what's come down to us today*[^1] — because it withdraws the exemption from the living versions of all three.

## The Actual Mechanism, and It Is Not About Effort

Then comes the sentence that makes this a page rather than a warning, and it is easy to read past because it arrives as an aside about why the old schools succeeded:

> They **didn't have to make any prior assumptions about what the end points of spiritual practice looked like**, and so they didn't attempt to try to bring these end goals into the path in order to try to force them into transpiring.[^1]

Read that backwards and you have the recipe for manufacturing a semblance dharma.

**Step one: acquire a description of the destination.** Read what the attainment is like — the stillness, the light, the dissolution, whatever the tradition specifies.

**Step two: take the description as a target.** Aim at it.

**Step three: succeed.** Produce, by effort, a state that matches the description.

That is the mechanism, and it is not a failure of sincerity or of effort — it is a failure caused *by* having good information and applying it diligently. The better the description, the better the counterfeit. The harder you work, the more convincing it gets.

Which is why the schools that avoided it did so not by trying harder but by **not knowing what they were aiming at**. Letting everything happen naturally, without force, without prior assumptions about the end point.[^1] You cannot manufacture what you cannot picture.

## The Trap That Closes: Descriptions Sound Alike

The second passage is where the problem becomes epistemically vicious rather than merely practical.

Bodri is distinguishing the Taoist *yin shen* emanation from the Buddhist thought-born body — two attainments that sound nearly identical in description, and which he says differ substantially in capability, control and what else they correspond to. Then:

> To confuse the yin shen with the thought-born body would be to mistake a semblance dharma for the real thing, and yet **if no one told you this, there would be no way for you to know because the descriptions sound so similar.**[^2]

*There would be no way for you to know.*

So the counterfeit is not detectable by comparison against the description — because the counterfeit was **built from** the description and matches it. What separates them is information that lives outside the description entirely, in someone's testimony.

And this cluster has already established what happens to testimony. The master may be mistaken and there is no way to check. The committee cannot certify. Self-assessment is the least reliable instrument available.

**So the one thing that could distinguish a semblance dharma from the real attainment is the one thing the tradition cannot supply reliably.** Bodri states both halves, four hundred pages apart, and never puts them together.

## Implementation Workflow

Here is the awkward part, and it should be said before any technique: **reading a good description of an attainment makes you more likely to manufacture it, not less.** That is the mechanism above, and it applies to this page, this hub, and the book they come from.

So the first move is not a practice, it is a handling rule. When you read an account of a state, note the *conditions* and skip the *phenomenology*. What did they do, for how long, in what circumstances. Not what it felt like. The felt account is the template a semblance dharma gets built from.

Now the test, which is the one instrument this material actually gives you. **Stop maintaining it.** Whatever you have, let it go for a fortnight — no arranging, no protecting, no special conditions. A semblance dharma is defined as something that can only be held in place by force; anything held that way will not survive being dropped, and anything that survives being dropped was not held.

You do not have to know what you have. You only have to stop holding it and see what is still there.

Then the diagnostic for the practice itself. Ask whether you are *aiming at a described state*. If the honest answer is yes — if you have a picture of where this is going and you are steering toward the picture — the mechanism says the steering is the problem, and it will feel exactly like diligence right up until the point where it succeeds.

And the humbler version for ordinary weeks: notice how much of your sitting is spent checking whether the thing has arrived. Checking requires a template. The template is the counterfeit's blueprint.

## Analytical Case Study: The Ranking That Cannot Be Applied

The *yin shen* case rewards being worked through slowly, because it shows exactly how much apparatus is needed to make the distinction and how little of it is available.

Bodri holds that the thought-born body is *much more advanced* than the *yin shen* emanation, and he gives three criteria for the difference: the thought-born body has **many more capabilities**, is **completely under your control**, and **corresponds to other advanced attainments involving detachment**.[^2]

Look at how those three would have to be used.

**Capabilities** — you would need to know the full range of what the real one can do, which means having a complete inventory from somewhere.

**Control** — this one is checkable and is the strongest. He notes that the newly born *yin shen* cannot be let far because it cannot be controlled well, and that letting it wander while the physical body is unprotected can end with the body buried or cremated in your absence.[^2] Whatever one makes of the claim, *degree of control* is an operational criterion.

**Correspondence** — you would need to verify a set of other attainments in order to verify this one, which is a regress.

So of three criteria, one is usable and two require knowledge the practitioner does not have. And Bodri's own sentence concedes the outcome: *if no one told you this, there would be no way for you to know*.[^2]

What that leaves is a ranking that is real, specific, and **not applicable by the person who needs it**. The distinction exists in the literature and cannot be operated from inside a practice — which is a very precise description of the position this whole cluster keeps arriving at from different directions.

## Why the Simple Method Loses

There is a second-order effect Bodri names on the same page, and it explains why semblance dharmas are common rather than rare.

> The simplest way is usually the highest and most direct way in the practice of spiritual cultivation. However, people usually go searching for something more complicated because the highest methods are so simple and thus "boring." Because they're so simple, people always doubt that they really work.[^1]

Put this beside the mechanism and a selection pressure appears that neither statement carries alone.

The methods least likely to produce a counterfeit are the ones with no target and no forcing — which means they produce **no visible progress and no interim phenomena**. The methods most likely to produce a counterfeit are elaborate, effortful, and generate results you can notice.

So a practitioner choosing between them, honestly and on the evidence available, will choose the one that manufactures the likeness. Not from vanity. From the entirely reasonable position that a method producing nothing observable is indistinguishable from a method that does not work.

**The counterfeit-producing method is selected for by exactly the diligence that ought to protect against it**, and there is no signal available to the chooser that would reverse the preference.

## What the Category Costs

Two things should be said against the concept, because it is powerful enough to be dangerous.

**It is unfalsifiable in the hands of a critic.** Any attainment anyone reports can be reclassified as a semblance dharma, on the grounds that the descriptions sound alike. Bodri uses it that way — the scope of *semblance* in his hands covers a great deal of what other traditions call arrival. The concept as he states it supplies no test that a third party could run, only a category.

**And it is not clearly separable from the sudden-and-gradual dispute.** The schools he says escaped the problem are the ones that reject staged, technique-driven practice. The schools he says produce semblance dharmas are the ones that use it. That mapping is suspiciously tidy, and it means the doctrine may be doing partisan work — a technical name for *the other schools' results* — rather than describing a phenomenon that shows up everywhere.

What survives both objections is the mechanism, which does not depend on his classification. **A described endpoint plus forceful effort produces a likeness of the endpoint.** That is a claim about method rather than about schools, and it applies to anyone with a good book and a strong will.

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

**Strongest support.** The mechanism is stated positively, as an explanation of why certain schools *avoided* the problem, rather than as an accusation — *they didn't have to make any prior assumptions about what the end points looked like*.[^1] An account arrived at from the success side is worth more than the same claim arrived at from the failure side.

**The tension the source does not close.** The only thing that distinguishes a semblance dharma from the real attainment is someone telling you,[^2] and the same book establishes at length that the someone cannot be verified. The category identifies a failure and locates its remedy in a faculty the book says is unavailable.

**A second tension.** The schools said to avoid semblance dharmas are the ones that reject staged technique — and this book is six hundred pages of staged technical description. Its own genre is the one the mechanism indicts.

**A third, on scope.** The category has no third-party test and can absorb any reported attainment. `[SINGLE SOURCE]` on the classification as applied to specific schools.

**And the standing scope limit.** The genuine attainments a semblance dharma imitates are stations on a ladder footnote 518 calls false stages.[^3] A counterfeit of a rest stop is an odd object, and the source does not comment on it.

**Open questions.** Is there any criterion for semblance dharmas that a practitioner could apply without external testimony, other than the persistence test? And does the mechanism predict something checkable — should traditions with more detailed phenomenological literature produce more counterfeits than traditions with less?

## Author Tensions & Convergences

Against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-book-that-warns-against-its-own-genre|The Book That Warns Against Its Own Genre]], this page supplies the technical name for the thing that book is worried about. That page observes that a catalogue of recorded results sits inside a book arguing that readers turn recorded results into methods. *Semblance dharma* is what the resulting product is called — which means the two pages are one argument, and the argument's target is the volume containing both.

The convergence with [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-unproduced-is-the-test|The Unproduced Is the Test]] is exact and supplies the remedy the category otherwise lacks. A semblance dharma is defined as maintainable only by force; the permanence criterion asks what survives the withdrawal of effort. **The unproduced test is the only semblance-dharma detector in the build that needs nobody's testimony**, and neither page states that connection.

Read with [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/verification-and-its-broken-chain|Verification and Its Broken Chain]], the loop closes badly and the pairing is the point. This page's counterfeits are detectable only by someone telling you; that page's tellers cannot be verified. A practitioner is therefore exposed to a failure mode whose only named remedy has already been shown unreliable.

Against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/samadhi-states-are-images-of-emptiness|Samādhi States Are Images of Emptiness]], the relationship is subtler than it looks. That page says the state is a representation because a mind produced it. This one says a specific class of state is a representation because a *description* produced it. The first is ontological and applies to everything; the second is causal and applies to a subset — and only the second implies that a different method would have avoided it.

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**Imitate the process and you learn; imitate the result and you counterfeit** — [[ARCHIVES/concepts/creative-practice/voice-cultivation-through-stylistic-models|Voice Cultivation Through Stylistic Models]]. That page's claim is unambiguous and runs the opposite way to this one: you do not find a voice, you build it by studying people better than you — identifying which master solved which structural problem, understanding exactly how, and practising the solution until it is instinct. Deliberate imitation is *the* method, and it works. So why does the same operation produce a counterfeit here? **The difference is what is being copied.** Dan Wang copies Stendhal's handling of irony and Rossini's repetition-with-variation — mechanisms, at the level of how the effect is produced. A practitioner reading a phenomenological account of samādhi copies the *finished surface*: what the state felt like, with no access to what generated it. **What the pairing gives that neither side gives alone: imitation is a training method when the model exposes its mechanism and a counterfeiting method when it exposes only its output — and contemplative literature is almost entirely output.** That is a sharper account of the imitation hazard than *don't have expectations*, and it yields a usable rule: from any account of an attainment, take the conditions and discard the phenomenology, because the conditions are the mechanism and the phenomenology is the surface. It also predicts where the hazard concentrates — in traditions whose literature is richest in experiential description, which is not where most people would look for it.

*One handshake.* The obvious second — a mimicked signal in an arms race — is carried in this hub by the *Source Mirror* page's withholding argument, and a version here would restate it.

## The Live Edge

**Sharpest implication.** **The counterfeit is built out of the description of the real thing, which means the better a tradition documents its attainments the better the forgeries it manufactures — and the reader who studies hardest is the one best equipped to produce one.**

**Generative questions.**
- Does the mechanism predict a measurable pattern — more counterfeits in traditions with richer phenomenological literature, fewer in traditions that withhold description?
- Other than the persistence test, is there any semblance-dharma criterion a practitioner can apply without someone else's testimony?
- If the remedy is not having a picture of the destination, what is a six-hundred-page description of the destination for?

# Sneha, Māna, Praṇaya, Rāga, Anurāga, Bhāva, Mahābhāva

## Seven Words for Love After Love

Most systems stop at love. This one treats `prema` as a floor and builds seven storeys on top of it.

**`Sneha`** — affection. **`Māna`** — a particular kind of indignation. **`Praṇaya`** — intimacy. **`Rāga`** — passion. **`Anurāga`** — continually renewed attachment. **`Bhāva`** — here meaning something above all of those. **`Mahābhāva`** — the great emotion, found in its highest form in one person.

That is the standard Gauḍīya list, and it is quoted in this book on the page facing Text 13.

And Text 13's own root text — Viśvanātha's Sanskrit, the thing the book is nominally an abstract *of* — gives a different list, in a different order, with one term missing.

That discrepancy is the spine of this page, and it is checkable in four lines of Sanskrit.

## What the Root Text Actually Says

Viśvanātha's Text 13, in full, is five sentences:

> The mature stage of `bhāva-bhakti` is called `prema`. Its symptom is that even when obstacles are present, **there is not even the slightest diminution.** A superior condition of `prema`, marked by an increase of `mamatā`, is known as **`sneha`**; its symptom is the melting of the heart. Superior to this is **`rāga`**, symptomised by intensified, condensed `sneha`. Superior to this is **`praṇaya`**, whose symptom is deep faith.[^1]

Four terms: `prema` → `sneha` → `rāga` → `praṇaya`. And it stops.

Now the list quoted in the Comment on the very next page, from Viśvanātha's own commentary on *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* 1.4.1:

> When `prema` matures, it gradually increases and takes the forms of **`sneha`, `māna`, `praṇaya`, `rāga`, `anurāga`, `bhāva` and `mahābhāva`.**[^2]

Set them side by side.

**Root:** sneha → **rāga** → **praṇaya**.
**Commentary:** sneha → māna → **praṇaya** → **rāga** → anurāga → bhāva → mahābhāva.

`Rāga` and `praṇaya` are **inverted.** `Māna` is **absent from the root entirely.** And the root stops at four where the commentary runs to eight.

Same author. Facing pages. One edition.

## How Much Weight the Discrepancy Bears

Before drawing anything from it, the honest limits.

**This may be an abstract's compression.** The *Bindu* is a summary, and a summarist may name three escalations as representative and stop. The root does not say *these are all*.

**The commentary quoted is on a different text.** It is Viśvanātha glossing Rūpa's *Sindhu*, not Viśvanātha glossing his own *Bindu*. He is reporting the standard scheme in one place and composing a compressed one in the other.

**And the order in the root is internally motivated.** `Rāga` is defined there as `nibiḍa-sneha` — *condensed `sneha`* — which makes it the natural next term after `sneha`, since it is `sneha` intensified. Put `praṇaya` between them and you have inserted *deep faith* into the middle of a density gradient. **The root's order is the one that follows from the root's own definitions.**

So the finding is not *Viśvanātha contradicted himself.* It is narrower and more interesting: **the *Bindu*'s compressed scheme is ordered by its own stated mechanism, and the standard scheme is not, and the book prints both without comment.** `[n=1 OBSERVED]`, and the decisive test lies in Rūpa's *Sindhu* and the *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*, neither of which this build has read.

## The Definitions the Root Does Give

Take the four the root actually defines, because they are unusually terse and each is a single diagnostic.

**`Prema`** — *no diminution even in the presence of obstacles.* The test is a stress test. Not intensity, not warmth: **whether an impediment reduces it.**

**`Sneha`** — *the melting of the heart*, `citta-dravībhāva`, and marked by an increase of `mamatā`. From solid to liquid, and the driver is possessiveness.

**`Rāga`** — *`nibiḍa-sneha`*, condensed or dense affection. Melted, then concentrated.

**`Praṇaya`** — *`gāḍha-viśvāsa`*, deep faith.

Read as a sequence, the first three are **states of matter**: unbroken, melted, condensed. And then the fourth changes register entirely — from a physics of the heart to an epistemic relation, *faith*.

Which is worth noticing because it is where the terse scheme becomes something other than a gradient. `Praṇaya` is not more of what `rāga` is more of. It is a different property arriving on top.

## Māna, and Why Losing It Matters

The missing term is the one worth mourning, because `māna` is the strangest item on the standard list.

`Māna` is the beloved's indignation — the sulk, the refusal, the withheld reconciliation. In the tradition's own narrative material it is what Rādhā does when she will not be placated, and it is counted as a **higher** state than the affection beneath it.

An escalation of love whose content is refusal is a genuinely unusual doctrinal object, and any scheme that drops it loses the most distinctive claim on the list.

This book names `māna` in the quoted list and never defines it. Its full treatment belongs to the *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi*, which the tradition holds as the authority for everything in this region — and which this build has not read and will make no claims about.

Which is a fair description of what Text 13 is: **a scheme that gestures at seven storeys, defines three, and points at another book for the rest.**

## The Structural Point the Root Does Make

For all its compression, the root supplies one thing the standard list does not: a **mechanism** for the ascent.

Every escalation it defines is driven by `mamatā`. *A superior condition of `prema` is **marked by an increase of `mamatā`.*** And `mamatā` is glossed immediately: *a deep sense of attachment or possessiveness in relation to Śrī Kṛṣṇa by which one thinks, "Kṛṣṇa is mine."*

So on the *Bindu*'s account, the ladder above `prema` is not a ladder of intensity, purity or duration.

**It is a ladder of possessiveness**, and each rung is a stronger claim of ownership over God.

That is a much more specific proposal than the standard list carries, and it is the compressed scheme's real contribution. It also explains why `śānta-rasa` — which the same book says is *devoid of `mamatā`* — cannot climb: the ladder's own drive-shaft is missing at that rung.

## Implementation Workflow

You want to locate yourself on this.

The root gives one test that is actually runnable, and it belongs to the bottom rung: **`prema` shows no diminution in the presence of obstacles.** That is checkable retrospectively — not *how much do I feel* but *what happened to it the last time something got in the way.* Everything above it is defined by melting, condensing and faith, which are not states you can inspect on demand.

Second scene, and it is where the compressed scheme is useful. You are reading the standard seven-term list and finding it opaque.

The root supplies the through-line the standard list lacks. **Read the ascent as increasing `mamatā`** — a strengthening claim that he is mine — and the terms acquire a common axis. Whether that axis is the tradition's settled view is exactly what the discrepancy leaves open, and it is the *Bindu*'s own.

Third, and it is a caution about this whole territory. This book defines four terms and names eight, and the material above them belongs to another treatise. **A page on the upper reaches built from this source alone would be building on a summary that says it is one** — which is why this page states three definitions and stops, rather than filling seven headings from elsewhere.

## Analytical Case Study: A Summary Whose Compression Is Also an Argument

The interesting question is whether the root's scheme is a shortened version of the standard one or a different one.

Three pieces of evidence say *different*.

**The order follows the definitions.** `Rāga` as `nibiḍa-sneha` belongs next to `sneha`. The standard order puts `praṇaya` between them, and `praṇaya` is defined by faith rather than by density. The root's sequence is mechanically coherent; the standard sequence is not, on the root's own definitions.

**The mechanism is stated.** `Mamatā` increase is named as what drives the ascent. The standard list is presented as an enumeration with no stated driver.

**And the omission is not random.** The term dropped, `māna`, is the one that does not fit an increasing-possessiveness gradient — indignation is not more ownership, it is ownership asserting itself by withdrawal, which is a different move.

So the compression looks like a **reconstruction**: a scheme rebuilt around a single axis, with the terms that fit the axis kept in mechanically motivated order, and the one that doesn't left out.

Stated at the strength the evidence carries: three converging observations on one four-line passage. `[n=1 OBSERVED]` — one instance, and I am reporting it rather than naming a pattern about Viśvanātha's method. The decisive test is his own treatment of these terms in the *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa*, which the Introduction lists among his works and which this build has not read.

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

**Strongest support.** Both lists are printed in the same edition on facing pages, one as Text 13's root Sanskrit and one inside the Comment on it. The definitions of `prema`, `sneha`, `rāga` and `praṇaya` are Viśvanātha's own compressed Sanskrit, and the `mamatā` gloss is the 1993 *vṛtti*'s.

**Tension one, and it is the page.** `Rāga` and `praṇaya` are inverted between the two lists, and `māna` is absent from one. Neither the root, the commentary nor the 1993 layer remarks on it.

**Tension two.** The root defines four terms and names no others; the Comment names eight. A reader taking Text 13 as the *Bindu*'s account of the upper reaches gets three escalations, and the book's title promises a drop of an ocean.

**Tension three.** The ascent is driven by `mamatā`, and `śānta-rati` is defined by its absence. So the lowest of the five primary rasas is structurally unable to enter this scale at all — which is a second, independent way in which `śānta` fails to be the bottom rung of a continuous series, alongside the Pass 6 finding that its object is a different form of God.

**Open question.** What is `bhāva` doing as the sixth item on a list whose first rung is above `prema`, when `bhāva` is also the name of the state *below* `prema` that Text 12 defines? The same word occupies two positions on the same scale, and nothing in the range read distinguishes them.

## Author Tensions & Convergences

The vault's Bryant material treats the escalations above `prema` as the tradition's fine-grained account of love's intensification — a sequence of named states running up to `mahābhāva`, presented as the standard list.

What this book adds is that the standard list is not the only one **in its own author's hands**, and that a compressed version ordered on a different principle sits four lines away from it.

Which is a small thing with a general consequence for how this vault should handle such enumerations. Named sequences in this literature are usually reported as fixed, and here is a case — in one edition, by one author, on facing pages — where the order moves and a term drops. **The list is not the doctrine; the mechanism is**, and where a mechanism is stated it is worth more than the enumeration it produces.

That converges with what the whole ingest keeps finding about this source: the enumerated surfaces are inherited and the arguments underneath them are the author's own.

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**A scale whose rungs are strengthening claims of ownership.** Set this against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/psychological-ownership-theory|Feeling Like Something Is Yours, Regardless of What the Paperwork Says]], whose claim is that felt ownership is a distinct psychological state from legal title — it arises from investment of the self, control, and intimate knowledge, and it generates the behaviours we associate with ownership regardless of whether any entitlement exists.

The *Bindu*'s compressed ladder is that state used as a **measuring axis for love** — each rung a stronger *Kṛṣṇa is mine*, in a case where legal title is not merely absent but conceptually impossible.

What the pair produces that neither yields alone. The ownership literature treats felt ownership as a phenomenon to be explained and, often, as a source of distortion — the endowment effect, the overvaluation, the disputes. This tradition treats it as **the thing that intensifies**, and grades devotional maturity by it.

Which puts a genuinely awkward question to both. If felt ownership arises from investment, control and intimate knowledge, then **a scale of increasing possessiveness toward God is a scale of increasing investment in something one cannot control** — and the ownership literature would predict exactly the outcome this tradition prizes: `māna`, the indignation of the one who feels entitled and is thwarted. The sulk is not a departure from possessiveness; it is what possessiveness does when it meets the uncontrollable.

Which suggests the term this scheme dropped is the one its own mechanism most strongly predicts, and that is a better reason to notice its absence than the inconsistency alone.

One handshake here rather than two. The order-discrepancy finding is the page's other half, and the vault's neighbours on taxonomy instability are about classification systems rather than about a single author's two orderings; a second connection there would rest on the resemblance of *list* to *list*.

## The Live Edge

**Sharpest implication.** The *Bindu*'s own scheme runs sneha → rāga → praṇaya, driven by increasing `mamatā`, and the standard scheme quoted on the facing page runs sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga. The compressed version is mechanically ordered and the standard one is not — and the term the compression drops is precisely the one that does not fit an ownership gradient.

**Generative questions.**
- Is the root's order a summarist's slip or a reconstruction around a stated axis? The definitions favour the second.
- If the ladder is graded by possessiveness, and `śānta` is defined by its absence, in what sense is `śānta` on the ladder at all?
- `Bhāva` names both the state below `prema` and the sixth rung above it. Which is the accident?

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/mamata-as-the-marker-of-prema|Mamatā as the Marker of Prema]] — the axis this ladder is graded on, and its absence in `śānta`
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/prema-does-not-abandon-its-earlier-stages|Prema Does Not Abandon Its Earlier Stages]] — why every rung stays available once reached
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/bhava-bhakti-as-a-ray-of-the-sun-of-prema|Bhāva-Bhakti as a Ray of the Sun of Prema]] — the state below `prema`, which shares a name with the sixth rung above it
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/twenty-three-of-twenty-seven|Twenty-Three of Twenty-Seven]] — the census that makes Text 13's root Viśvanātha's own composition rather than Rūpa's
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/madhurya-rasa-the-amorous-apex|Mādhurya Rasa — The Amorous Apex]] — the rasa in which these escalations are principally developed
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/santa-rasa|Śānta Rasa]] — the rasa the ladder's own drive-shaft is missing from

## Footnotes

[^1]: [[ARCHIVES/sources/visvanatha-bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu-bindu|Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu-bindu]] — Text 13, root text, Viśvanātha's own Sanskrit (c. 1690s) — `mamatvātiśayāt premṇa eva uparitano 'vasthā viśeṣaḥ snehaḥ… tato rāgaḥ… tataḥ praṇayaḥ`. Translation as given in the *Śrī Bindu-vikāśinī-vṛtti*, 1993.
[^2]: Same source, Text 13, Comment, quoting Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura's commentary on *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu* 1.4.1 in translation. The same seven-term list is repeated at Text 14. `[n=1 OBSERVED]` on the discrepancy; the decisive test lies in Rūpa's *Sindhu* and in Viśvanātha's *Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa*, neither read in this build.

# The Funnel of the Fortunate

## The Slide With the Big Number at the Top

Somebody puts up a slide. At the top there is an enormous number — everyone in the country, everyone on the platform, everyone who could conceivably want this. Then it narrows. Those who have heard of us. Those who visited. Those who signed up. Those who stayed.

At the bottom there is a small number, and the small number is where you are, or where the speaker wants you to be.

You have seen a hundred of these and you know exactly what they do to a room. The top number makes the bottom one feel earned. Nobody in the audience checks whether any of the intermediate figures were counted or estimated, because that is not the part doing the work. **The work is done by the shape.**

Madhya 19 has one, and it starts at eight million four hundred thousand.

## The Descent

The count runs downward in steps, and each step throws away most of what was left.[^1]

Eight million four hundred thousand species of life. Of those, the ones that move. Of those, human beings. Of those, the ones who follow Vedic principle. Of those, the half who are not merely paying lip service to it. Of those, the ones who act rather than talk. Of those, the wise. Of those, the liberated.

And out of many millions of liberated souls — that is, out of the survivors of every previous cut, each of whom has already achieved what most of Indian religion regards as the finish line — **one is a pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa.**

Read that last step twice, because it is where the passage stops being a survey of the world and becomes an argument about this tradition. The funnel does not narrow to *the religious*. It narrows past liberation, and then narrows again.

## What the Shape Is Doing

Take the numbers away and the passage still works, which tells you the numbers are not the mechanism.

The mechanism is that the reader arrives at the bottom of the funnel with the tradition. **You are reading this page, so you are already through the last cut but one** — and the pressure of the passage is entirely on the gap between where you have got to and the single figure at the end.

It is not a threat and it is not a promise. It is a placement. The passage tells you where you are standing and how few people are standing there, and it does that before making any claim about what you should do next.

Which is why the sequence matters more than the arithmetic. Each step is an entire category of human seriousness — literacy, discipline, wisdom, liberation — dismissed as a landing on the way down. **By the time the last step arrives, the reader has watched every rival attainment get spent as small change.**

## The Numbers Are Not Measurements

Worth saying plainly, because the passage is often read as though it were reporting.

None of these figures is derived. The eight million four hundred thousand is a traditional number, not a census. The "half who merely pay lip service" is not a proportion anybody counted. And the last ratio — millions of liberated souls to one pure devotee — is unavailable to anybody, since the corpus's own doctrine holds that liberation and devotion are both interior conditions that cannot be read off from conduct.[^2]

So the passage is stating, as demography, a claim whose terms are by its own account unobservable.

That is not a gotcha. It is a description of what kind of statement this is. **It is a ranking wearing a headcount**, and the headcount is doing rhetorical work the ranking could not do alone — because a ranking invites you to argue about the order, and a number does not invite anything.

## Analytical Case Study: The Step That Is Not Demographic

Every cut in the funnel except one narrows a population by a property people could in principle be sorted on. Moving or not moving. Human or not. Following a practice or not.

The last cut is different, and the difference is the page.

**Liberated to pure devotee is not a narrower slice of the same thing.** The corpus is explicit elsewhere that the desire for liberation is a competing goal, a weed, a plant that consumes the same water — not an earlier stage of devotion but a different plant.[^3]

Which means the funnel is doing something illegitimate at exactly its most important step. Steps one through seven narrow a set. Step eight **switches to a different set entirely** and presents the switch as further narrowing.

The rhetorical payoff of that switch is large. Presented as a fork, the tradition has to argue for its road against a serious rival. Presented as the last step of a funnel, the rival road is not a rival — it is the second-to-last landing, and everyone on it is simply not there yet.

The corpus makes both claims and never puts them together.

## The Reader Is Always at the Bottom

There is a structural fact about funnels that the corpus's version inherits and does not mention.

**Nobody ever reads themselves into the middle.** The person hearing this passage is, by construction, someone who has encountered the tradition and is paying attention — so the passage's early cuts cost them nothing. They pass through the first seven steps in a sentence.

Which makes the funnel a device that flatters and pressures with the same motion. You are told that you are, statistically, almost nobody — and the near-nobody status is granted for free, on the strength of listening.

And the scarcity is unfalsifiable in the direction that matters. If the pure devotee is one in millions, then any given community containing very few of them is exactly what the doctrine predicts. **A movement can be almost entirely composed of people who have not arrived, and the number at the bottom of the funnel explains that in advance.**

## The Layers

Layer A gives the descent compactly, as a chain of steps inside the instruction, without arithmetic and without a moral attached.[^4]

Layer B tends to press the scarcity into an argument about the rarity and therefore the value of the association the reader has been fortunate enough to find.[^5]

The direction of the expansion is worth marking. **The verse's funnel ends in a statement about how few pure devotees there are. The commentary's tends to end in a statement about how fortunate the reader is to be near one.** The first is a claim about the world; the second is a claim about the reader's present circumstances, and it is not in the verse.

## Implementation Workflow

Somebody shows you a funnel and the bottom number is where you are. **Look at whether every step narrows the same set.** One of them usually does not, and that is the step the whole diagram was built to smuggle — the point where a competing option gets redrawn as an earlier stage of yours.

You are being told how rare this is. **Ask who could have counted.** If the defining property is invisible by the speaker's own account, the number is not evidence, and knowing that does not make the claim false — it makes it a claim of a different kind, which you should weigh differently.

You have been placed near the bottom of somebody's descent and it feels good. **Notice that you were placed there for free**, on the strength of being in the room. Nothing was checked. The flattery and the pressure arrived in the same sentence and they are the same sentence.

You are running a group that is supposed to produce a rare outcome and mostly does not. **A scarcity doctrine explains that away permanently**, which is a real service and a real hazard, and the hazard is that no rate of failure can ever count as news.

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

The evidence is a compact descending chain inside the instruction to Rūpa Gosvāmī, stated without argument and without any attempt to source its figures.[^6]

**The tension the source doesn't close: the last step of the funnel contradicts the corpus's own account of liberation.** Here it is the penultimate landing on one road; three verses of the same instruction set have it as a competing goal that consumes the practitioner's resources. It cannot be both a stage and a rival.

**A second one.** The passage runs on a distinction — liberated versus devoted — that this corpus insists is interior and unverifiable. The demography requires exactly the kind of observation the epistemology forbids.

**Open:** whether the corpus ever states the funnel and the fork together. Nothing in the range read does, and the two framings support very different attitudes to everybody outside the tradition.

## Author Tensions & Convergences

This page sits against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-plundered-storehouse|The Plundered Storehouse]] as hard as anything in the corpus does. There, the treasury is broken open and distributed *"not considering who was a fit candidate and who was not."* Here, the arithmetic says one in many millions. **Unlimited distribution and vanishing yield, in one book, about one commodity** — and the corpus never asks what happens to the plundered storehouse's contents in a world where almost nobody ends up holding any.

It supplies the demographic version of [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-weeds-beside-the-creeper|The Weeds Beside the Creeper]]'s doctrinal claim. That page has liberation as a competing plant; this one has it as the second-to-last step. The two are the same corpus's two ways of handling the same rival, and the choice between them appears to be governed by what the passage is trying to do rather than by anything settled.

And it is the pessimistic pole of the entry material. The accident story and the instant-guarantee story sit in the next chapter of the same instruction; those pages are `the-log-on-the-river` and the surrender material, and the three do not reconcile.

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**[[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/false-scarcity|False Scarcity]]** — that page's mechanism is an artificial limit producing a real behavioural change. A "Limit 12 per customer" sign on soup raises average purchases from 5.6 cans to 7, with no change to actual supply. A "Sold Out" label raises perceived value even when the item is in stock. The scarcity is manufactured; the effect is not.

The corpus's funnel produces the same effect and it does not do the same thing, and the gap between them is the finding.

In every case the scarcity literature examines, **somebody restricts supply.** A limit is imposed, a label applied, stock withheld. That is what makes the manipulation detectable — you can go and look at the warehouse, and the discrepancy between the warehouse and the sign is the evidence.

Here nothing is restricted. **A number is published**, about a property nobody can observe, concerning a good the same corpus describes as distributed without conditions. There is no supply-side act to catch. The soup is not being withheld; the reader is being told how few people ever get soup.

Which gives the general finding neither page reaches. **Scarcity does not require a restrictor.** It requires only a credible statement about how many, and where the defining property is unobservable, that statement can never be checked against a warehouse. The scarcity literature's standard defence — look at what the seller is actually doing with the supply — has no purchase at all on the version that operates by assertion, and the assertion version is the one every ideology uses.

## The Live Edge

**Sharpest implication.** A funnel is an argument disguised as a measurement, and its load-bearing step is always the one where the set quietly changes. Here that step converts the tradition's most serious rival into its own second-to-last landing, and the conversion is invisible because it arrives wearing the same shape as the seven steps before it.

**Generative questions.**
- Does this corpus ever state the funnel and the fork in the same place? If not, is the choice between them rhetorical or doctrinal?
- If the distinguishing property is unobservable, what would it take for a scarcity claim about it to be wrong?
- Unlimited distribution and one-in-millions yield are both asserted here about one substance. Which of the two does the tradition actually operate on?

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-weeds-beside-the-creeper|The Weeds Beside the Creeper]] — liberation as a rival plant rather than a landing
